A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete and readable, including v2 Appendices A–E; v1 has no separate appendix. Despite the changed title and scope, the shared EmoAva dataset, CTEG method, and matching experimental results establish continuity of the research.

before.justification: V1 reports original CTEG experiments on EmoAva, human preference evaluations, ablations, and GiGA rendering experiments on NeRSemble.

after.justification: V2 retains original CTEG experiments and adds listener-dataset results, architecture studies, and qualitative examples in its appendices.

M1.justification: V2 removes the GiGA rendering method, including its offset-aware module and two-stage optimization from v1 Section 6. CTEG's autoregressive CVAE, EwA, LTA, and target-guided loss remain unchanged. The additional CTEG variants are experimental investigations rather than replacements for the main method.

E1.justification: The 15,000-pair English EmoAva dataset is retained. V2 removes NeRSemble avatar-reconstruction evaluation and adds evaluation on the LM-Listener dataset, described as containing a single character and listener expressions. This substantially changes the evaluated tasks and populations.

E2.justification: The GiGA comparisons against GaussianAvatars and PointAvatar are removed entirely. CTEG retains LM-Listener, Shuffle, and Random as comparators. The added listener-dataset experiment uses the existing LM-Listener comparator; newly cited DiffListener is not evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 removes the multiview self-reenactment protocol, rendering metrics, and two-stage training settings in v1 Section 7.2. Appendix C adds listener-dataset evaluation using L2, FD, Variation, and P-FD, plus controlled architecture and decoder-depth experiments. The retained main CTEG training budget and human-study sample settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds projection-sharing, attention-versus-pooling, BERT fine-tuning, and decoder-depth studies, plus additional expression case studies. It retains the original CTEG component ablations, KL-collapse analysis, and latent-cluster visualization. GiGA's sparsity sensitivity and triangle-influence analyses are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report CTEG standard errors using 1,000 bootstrap iterations, with identical uncertainty values in the retained main tables. V2 extends uncertainty reporting to additional results but documents no new run counts, seed protocol, significance tests, or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 3 retain identical numerical results. V2 adds listener-dataset results, including L2 of 0.37 for CTEG versus 0.43 for LM-Listener in Table 5, alongside variant, depth, and qualitative findings. V1's GiGA results in Table 4 and associated rendering and sensitivity findings are removed.

T1.justification: V1's formal 3DAR problem and GiGA definitions for pulling triangles, sparse attention, Gaussian offsets, and optimization are removed. CTEG's Gaussian assumptions, generation equations, and losses remain, as do the FgD, DoT, and Cppl definitions relocated to v2 Appendix D.

C1.justification: V2 reframes the contribution from an Emo3D benchmark and two-method avatar-generation system to a claimed first end-to-end text-to-expression model supported by EmoAva. GiGA's rendering and micro-expression claims disappear, while CTEG's empirical claims expand to include an existing listener dataset.

C2.justification: V2 adds English-only and personalization limitations, interpretations of projection sharing and BERT fine-tuning, and a proposed cumulative-sampling explanation for depth-related instability. It removes GiGA's mechanism discussion and v1's explicit qualifications concerning the human-preference gap to ground truth and LM-Listener's incompatibility with Cppl.

D1.justification: V2 adds preprocessing and source-screening details, annotator compensation, planned separate video and expression-code licenses, unshared-projection disclosure, and single-A100 hardware with fewer than 130M parameters. These expand documentation without establishing changed EmoAva construction. GiGA-specific implementation and optimization details are removed.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts substantially from general 3D generation and reconstruction toward emotional talking heads and text-driven motion. GiGA's relationship to GaussianAvatars and much associated literature disappear. V2 adds references including MotionGPT, DiffListener, and CelebV-Text, and expands dataset-source comparisons in Appendix B.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The main narrative is reorganized around CTEG, with dataset details, metric formulas, and visualizations moved into appendices. Dedicated limitations and ethical-considerations sections are added.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the overview and adds dataset-comparison, listener-result, and variant tables, plus construction, depth-study, and qualitative figures. GiGA displays and the dataset distribution plots disappear. Existing displays are extensively relocated, including v1 Figure 7 becoming v2 Figure 10, and the document adopts a different page format.

improvement.justification: The additional listener-dataset comparison and architecture studies better support the retained CTEG contribution, while expanded dataset documentation and explicit applicability limits make it easier to assess. These provide a modest net benefit. The tradeoffs are narrower scope through removal of the independently evaluated GiGA contribution and loss of useful earlier result qualifications; the main EmoAva results themselves are unchanged.
